audit_findings.title: Material litigation judgments are unaccrued claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: Gemini seeks $18.6 million; the Ontario action claims CAD$50 million general and CAD$100 million punitive damages plus unspecified amounts; OE impact otherwise unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An uninsured judgment or settlement would reduce the equity bridge directly; recurring defense costs would reduce owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: After consultation with litigation counsel and a review of the merit of each claim, we have concluded that we are unable to reasonably estimate the probability or the estimated range of reasonably possible losses related to material adverse judgments related to such claims and, therefore, we have not accrued for any such judgments.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not a demonstrated accounting or valuation error because loss probability and an estimable loss range remain unresolved. It is nevertheless material: the $18.6 million Gemini demand alone equals 7.8% of the $239 million base equity value and $0.40 per diluted share, while the certified Ontario claim is substantially larger. The existing $3.6 million product-litigation reserve covers expected defense costs, not adverse judgments.
audit_findings.action: Build the requested case-level matrix, identify applicable insurance and captive limits and retentions, obtain current counsel probability assessments, and rerun each scenario with probability-weighted uninsured judgments and ongoing defense costs.

audit_findings.title: Prospective capital intensity may be undercharged in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest forecast is $45.0-$50.0 million of FY2027 capital expenditures, with $11.929 million spent in Q1; forecast spending equals 2.8-3.1 times the $16.1 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any maintenance, replacement, or compliance portion exceeding the recurring capital charge embedded in the anchor must be deducted from forecast owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: We currently expect to spend $40.0 to $45.0 million on capital expenditures in fiscal 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large prospective spending requirement but does not classify it between maintenance and growth. It therefore does not prove the anchor is wrong. The scale is material: even a minority of the $45-$50 million program treated as incremental recurring maintenance could consume a substantial portion of the $16.1 million anchor, while deducting the full increase over FY2026 capital spending could eliminate modeled owner earnings.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2027 spending by project and economic purpose, determine normalized recurring maintenance capital, and rerun all scenarios using that charge in the anchor and forecast years.

audit_findings.title: FY2026 sell-in substantially outpaced the stated consumer-demand indicator
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 handgun sell-in exceeded the demand indicator by 19.2 percentage points; Q1 FY2027 sell-in exceeded it by 12.0 points; dollar OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary distributor loading can inflate the OE anchor and lead the growth scenarios to project revenue and margins that later reverse through destocking or promotions.
audit_findings.evidence: Handgun unit shipments into the sporting goods channel increased 19.0% over fiscal 2025, while overall consumer demand decreased 0.2% (as indicated by adjusted background checks for handguns reported to the National Instant Criminal Background Check System, or NICS).
audit_findings.explanation: The divergence is demonstrated, and it persisted into Q1 FY2027, but it does not by itself prove channel inventory accumulation. New products represented 38.1% of FY2026 sales and 35.3% of Q1 FY2027 sales, so durable market-share gains or product mix could explain part of the gap. Distributor inventory and sell-through data are absent, preventing a supported OE adjustment or materiality conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain distributor inventory, weeks-of-supply, sell-through, returns, cancellations, promotions, and subsequent orders; then normalize the anchor and growth rates for any identified loading or destocking cycle.

audit_findings.title: The Missouri lease creates contingent guaranty exposure distinct from ordinary debt principal
audit_findings.magnitude: April 30 future lease payments were $46.173 million versus $45.548 million of scheduled AOUT payments; present values were $34.021 million and $33.441 million, a $0.580 million reported mismatch; gross contingent exposure remains unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If AOUT stops paying, SWBI could incur lease cash outflows despite the valuation treating debt as context-only; those outflows would reduce OE or require an equity-bridge deduction net of recoveries.
audit_findings.evidence: We are a party to a material finance lease, which is a $46.2 million lease that has an effective interest rate of approximately 5.0% and is payable in 240 monthly installments through fiscal 2039, as well as a related payment and performance guaranty, dated October 26, 2017, in favor of the Original Missouri Landlord.
audit_findings.explanation: The current arrangement is substantially matched and AOUT paid the landlord directly during FY2025 and FY2026, so no present valuation error is demonstrated. The guaranty is an existing contractual exposure, however, and annual scheduled payments around $3.5 million would equal roughly 22% of the $16.1 million OE anchor if SWBI had to fund them. The record provides no evidence about AOUT default risk or recovery rights sufficient to establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Assess AOUT credit quality, guaranty enforceability, indemnification priority and collectability, and insurance; reconcile the lease liability to the matching asset and rerun only the probability-weighted uninsured or unrecoverable exposure.

audit_findings.title: Known environmental remediation has no recorded reserve
audit_findings.mechanism: Unreserved legacy cleanup costs would reduce the equity bridge when incurred as a discrete obligation; recurring remediation and compliance spending reduces owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: As of April 30, 2026, we did not have an open environmental reserve recorded in our consolidated balance sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: Known contamination, two Springfield release areas, two potentially responsible-party sites, possible joint-and-several liability, and the absence of an environmental reserve are demonstrated. They do not establish a misstatement or omitted amount because no probable cost range is supplied. FY2026 environmental compliance spending of $1.9 million, about 11.8% of the OE anchor, is already reflected in operating results; the incremental legacy-remediation exposure cannot be quantified from the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current site studies, regulator correspondence, remedial alternatives, cost and timing ranges, responsible-party allocations, and coverage; rerun OE for recurring costs and the bridge for probability-weighted uninsured legacy obligations.

audit_findings.title: The Tennessee incentive remains subject to a cash clawback
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum $9.0 million, equal to $0.19 per diluted share and 3.8% of the $239 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A required repayment would be a one-time cash claim reducing the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: If the three-year average number of full-time jobs during the Compliance Period is less than 50% of the committed number, we will be required to make a recapture payment equal to the full amount of the grant.
audit_findings.explanation: The clawback is conditional on 2027-2029 employment tests and no present breach is shown. Even the maximum repayment would reduce base value from $5.14 to approximately $4.95 per share and would not alter the conclusion relative to the $12.89 market price; a partial clawback would be smaller.
audit_findings.action: Monitor qualifying headcount and wages against the agreement definitions and confirm accrual treatment; rerun the bridge only if projected compliance falls below the applicable threshold.
